thread_analysis.thread_summary: NEC Platforms (NECPF) registration of 3 communications terminal models, all using the same Bluetooth chip and Fluoride 1.5 Host Stack (modified AOSP Fluoride). Company decided to align all model ICS to Fluoride 1.5 (not individual model feature sets). All 3 entered in one Product List under one registration. Key guidance: first product entered in Product List = Design Name; Allion recommended using a unified generic name (e.g., 'Communications Terminal') as the first entry. Profile tests exempt via referenced Fluoride 1.5 QDID. TCW applied. SIG fee payment was delayed by Lunar New Year holiday (Taiwan HQ through Feb 22). Registration completed with public release scheduled March 6.
all_questions_found: Can 3 models with the same chip and Host Stack share one registration? (→ case_01)
What name should be used for the registration Design Name — the first Product List entry? (→ case_01)
Google Fluoride 1.4/1.5/1.6 QDIDs produce fatal GAP/GATT Consistency Check Invalids with our module — why and what is the alternative? (→ case_02)
Compliance Folder for multi-model registration — one representative product's documents or documents for all 3 models? (→ case_03)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Multi-model registration under one Product List is a cost-efficient approach when models share the same Bluetooth implementation. ICS aligned to Host Stack rather than per-model features is acceptable and common. The Design Name rule (first Product List entry = Design Name) is a SIG portal behavior that is not prominently documented but has material consequences for branding and public listing. Profile test exemption via QDID reference eliminates the most expensive test category when a certified Host Stack QDID exists. Critically, Google LLC's Fluoride 1.4/1.5/1.6 QDIDs generate unresolvable GAP/GATT Consistency Check Invalids — the SIG added check rules after these QDIDs were registered, making them incompatible with the customer's module. NEC Platforms used their own customized AOSP Fluoride 1.5 (separate QDID), which does not have these Invalids.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Same chip + same Host Stack = one registration, multiple Product List entries. ICS = Host Stack capabilities. Design Name = first Product List entry (must be pre-planned). Profile test exempted by Host Stack QDID reference. Always trial-check QDID combinations for Consistency Check compatibility before paying any fees. Compliance Folder requires only one representative product's documents when all models share the same Bluetooth implementation.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Entering a model-specific name first causes that individual model name to become the public Design Name for the entire product family — not correctable after submission without SIG administrative involvement.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified. Allion proactively advised on the Design Name rule and guided NECPF to use a unified generic name as the first entry.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Three lessons from this thread: (1) The Design Name = first Product List entry rule is easy to overlook — always confirm the unified name before entering any products. (2) Never select a Host Stack QDID without first doing a trial Consistency Check in a temporary Qualification Workspace; Google Fluoride 1.x QDIDs are known to have post-registration GAP/GATT Invalids. (3) For multi-model registrations, proactively confirm that one representative product's Compliance Folder documents are sufficient — this saves the customer unnecessary effort.
